title: Design System: Money Monitor for iPhone

display.purpose: One leading financial amount per viewport.

motion.name: review-advance
motion.purpose: Moves a confirmed transaction out before revealing the next item.

motion.name: system-navigation
motion.purpose: Push, sheet, and tab transitions remain platform-owned.

components.name: Primary Review Button
components.description: The single full-width completion action in Review.
components.css: .ds-primary-review { width: 100%; min-height: 54px; border: 0; border-radius: 17px; background: #171914; color: #F5F3EE; font: 700 17px/1.2 system-ui; } .ds-primary-review:hover { opacity: .84; } .ds-primary-review:active { opacity: .72; } .ds-primary-review:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #68C697; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Attention Group
components.description: A contextual cluster used only when the current state deserves attention.
components.html: 3 transactions to reviewClean up your financial inbox
components.css: .ds-attention { display: grid; gap: 3px; padding: 16px 14px; border-radius: 16px; background: #FCFBF8; color: #171914; font-family: system-ui; } .ds-attention strong { font-size: 15px; } .ds-attention span { color: #656A61; font-size: 13px; }

components.name: Filter Chip
components.description: A 44-point Activity filter with a solid selected state.
components.css: .ds-filter-chip { min-height: 44px; padding: 0 14px; border: 0; border-radius: 22px; background: #171914; color: #F5F3EE; font: 600 13px system-ui; } .ds-filter-chip:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #68C697; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Budget Pace
components.description: Paired time and budget tracks that make pacing visible without a decorative chart.
components.css: .ds-budget { display: grid; gap: 10px; color: #656A61; font: 13px system-ui; } .ds-budget div { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 96px 1fr 36px; align-items: center; gap: 10px; } .ds-budget i { height: 5px; border-radius: 3px; background: linear-gradient(90deg, #216849 var(--p), #D8D7CF var(--p)); } .ds-budget b { color: #171914; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; text-align: right; }

components.name: Three-Tab Navigation
components.description: The stable Home, Activity, and Explore information architecture.
components.css: .ds-tabs { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); padding: 10px 0 14px; border-top: 1px solid #D8D7CF; background: #F8F6F2; font: 12px system-ui; text-align: center; } .ds-tabs a { color: #656A61; } .ds-tabs .active { color: #216849; font-weight: 600; } .ds-tabs a:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #68C697; outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview: Money Monitor feels like a private financial instrument: calm enough for daily use, precise enough to trust, and immediately useful without decoration. Hierarchy comes from the financial comparison itself, generous spacing, and a small number of native surfaces—not from a grid of interchangeable dashboard cards. The first screen states current spending, explains its pace, relates it to income and time elapsed, then surfaces only actionable changes.
keyCharacteristics: Warm neutral light mode and near-black olive dark mode.
One deep-green interaction voice, with amber and red reserved for financial meaning.
Large tabular financial numerals paired with plain-language comparisons.
Native iOS navigation, sheets, controls, SF Symbols, haptics, and system transitions.
Flat, hairline-separated structure with no decorative shadows or gradients.

rules.name: The Meaningful Color Rule
rules.body: Green, amber, and red describe interaction or financial state; they never decorate empty space.

rules.name: The One Statement Rule
rules.body: Only one financial value receives display scale in a viewport; comparisons explain it instead of competing with it.

rules.name: The Flat Ledger Rule
rules.body: Do not add card shadows, floating glass, or elevation to make ordinary content feel important.

dos: Do lead with a comparison that answers whether the current number is normal, improving, or worsening.
Do let Home say very little when accounts, budgets, and review state are healthy.
Do use SF Symbols and native iOS controls for familiar interaction.
Do use tabular numerals for money, percentages, and progress.
donts: Don't recreate the desktop dashboard or introduce permanent cards for operationally healthy state.
Don't use green, amber, or red without a financial or interaction meaning.
Don't add decorative charts, gradients, glass, shadows, achievement mechanics, or placeholder tabs.
Don't duplicate financial calculations on the phone; render the Mac's mobile projection.
